[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]
- Amount: 30
- Contributor(s): Linda Gorski
- Description: 30 minutes of Linda Gorski thinking through the cacao procurement process and advising Gary Teh on how to structure the arrangement commercially. Two substantive recommendations, posted in the 'Fans of Mulan!' family thread:
  
  (1) INSIST ON BEING FUNDED UP FRONT - 50% MINIMUM. Reasoning given by analogy: if a professional is not paid in advance it is very risky, because the customer can change his mind while the professional is already in the field (in this case Brazil). She illustrated with a family anecdote: her cousin John told Trump Jr 'Why would I want to do work for you again if you won't pay me the first time!' - after which Trump Jr paid quickly. Her conclusion: 'The customer should show that they are invested up front by paying at least 50%.' She notes 'Business is not like a family, although even families hold standards of honesty with each other.' Signed 'A wise Grandma who also made such types of mistakes in her life. Linda'.
  
  (2) CREATE A STANDING CONTRACT FOR THE PROCUREMENT-OF-CACAO TASK SET. Linda suggests Gary draft a dollar-denominated contract for the set of tasks he performs for the chocolate-buying customer. Because Gary already knows what is entailed, he is positioned to write a contract that is fair, covers the real cost of doing the work, and prices his time properly. Her stated purpose is protective: 'to keep Gary from the disappointment of customer betrayal by insisting on getting funded up front. It is more than fair to expect 50% fee up front. All our contractors expect this.' She adds 'Everyone has to set standards if they are in business.'
  
  Substantive proposal worth acting on: a standard Agroverse procurement/procurement-agent engagement contract with a 50% upfront deposit, scoped deliverables, and cost recovery. Relates to the outstanding cacao procurement workflow.
- Type: Time (Minutes)
--------
